title: Reduced-fibre theorem after a separable alteration of an integral base
statement: Let $S$ be an integral quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme], with generic point $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}k(S)$ [def-sc-generic-point]. Quasi-compact quasi-separated means that $S$ has a finite affine open covering whose pairwise intersections are quasi-compact. Let $f:X\to S$ be a dominant finitely presented morphism [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]; dominant means that its image is dense. Suppose its generic fibre $X_\eta$ is geometrically reduced, meaning that $X_\eta\times_{k(S)}\Omega$ is reduced for every field extension $\Omega/k(S)$ [def-pc-base-change, def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Then there are an integral scheme $S\prime$, a proper surjective morphism $r:S\prime\to S$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism] whose generic fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}L$ for a finite separable extension $L/k(S)$, and a finite morphism $q:Y\prime\to X\times_S S\prime$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] such that $q$ is an isomorphism over $\operatorname{Spec}L$. In this conclusion the finite generic modification means a finite (hence proper) map inducing an isomorphism on the generic fibre, as specified in the opening paragraph of Temkin §3.5; no schematically dense isomorphism open in the original nonflat target is asserted. Moreover $Y\prime\to S\prime$ is flat and finitely presented [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and all its geometric fibres [def-weil-geometric-fibre] are reduced. No normality, Noetherianity, dimension bound, or flatness of $f$ is assumed.

source.place: Theorem 3.5.5, printed p. 21 (PDF page 21), with the integral qcqs convention of §1.2, printed p. 3. Public primary PDF read online; local archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-eta-flatification] to $f$. Write $b:S_1\to S$ and $a:Z\to X\times_S S_1$ for its output. Properness makes $S_1$ qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](2): a proper map is quasi-compact and separated, hence quasi-separated. Thus $S_1$ is integral qcqs, $b$ is proper surjective with the original generic field $K=k(S)$, $a$ is finite and a generic isomorphism; moreover $Z\to S_1$ is flat and finitely presented. The generic fibre of $Z$ is identified with $X_\eta$, so it is geometrically reduced. It remains to construct a reduced-fibre finite generic modification of $Z$ after a separable alteration of $S_1$; no density in the original nonflat target is used.

source.place: Theorem 3.5.5, Step 0, printed pp. 21–22.

proof.text: Choose a finite affine cover $S_a=\operatorname{Spec}R_a$ of $S_1$ and, for each $a$, a finite affine cover $Z_{ab}=\operatorname{Spec}A_{ab}$ of $Z\times_{S_1}S_a$. Each $A_{ab}$ is a flat finitely presented $R_a$-algebra, by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-affine-criterion] and finite presentation of $Z\to S_1$; the affine restrictions remain of finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1). Fix a separable closure $L/K$. For every centred valuation ring $V\subseteq L$ over $S_a$, pull back $Z_{ab}$ to $V$. Flatness is preserved by [lem-pc-relatively-flat-module-pullback], applied to the structure sheaf, and finite presentation by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3). The generic algebra is geometrically reduced by [lem-trf-geometric-reduced-fibre-locus-base-change].

source.place: Theorem 3.5.5, Steps 1 and 5, printed pp. 22,24.

proof.text: For every $(a,b,V)$ apply [lem-trf-valuation-reduced-fibre-normalization] to $A_{ab}\otimes_{R_a}V$. The field $L$ is separably closed, and the preceding step checks flatness, finite presentation and geometric reducedness of the generic algebra. Its relative integral closure $B_{ab,V}$ is finite over $A_{ab}\otimes V$, flat and finitely presented over $V$, agrees with the original algebra after tensoring with $L$, and has reduced geometric fibres. This invokes the precise separably closed valuation-field theorem, including its arbitrary-height limit clause; it does not assert that the same construction works over an arbitrary valuation field.

source.place: Theorem 3.5.5, Steps 2–4 and valuation-limit part of Step 5, printed pp. 22–24.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-eta-modification-spreading] with $R=R_a$, the extension $L/K$, the valuation ring $V$, the algebra $A=A_{ab}$ and $B=B_{ab,V}$. It gives an integral affine $L$-quasi-model $U_{ab,V}=\operatorname{Spec}R'_{ab,V}\to S_a\to S_1$, a lift of $\operatorname{Spec}V$ to it, and a finite generically isomorphic map $Y_{ab,V}\to Z_{ab}\times_{S_a}U_{ab,V}$. The morphism $Y_{ab,V}\to U_{ab,V}$ is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] and finitely presented with reduced geometric fibres. All of these are outputs of the spreading statement; no unspecified neighbourhood or finite-type assumption on $S_1$ is inserted.

source.place: Theorem 3.5.5, Step 5 and §3.1, printed pp. 14–15,24.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-qcqs-separable-riemann-zariski-refinement]. For each fixed $(a,b)$ the opens $RZ_L(U_{ab,V})$ cover $RZ_L(S_a)$, since every valuation $V$ has the lift just constructed. Quasi-compactness gives a finite subfamily for this pair. There are finitely many pairs $(a,b)$, so one common $L$-model $T\to S_1$ refines all chosen quasi-models, with quasi-compact open subschemes $W_{abj}\subseteq T$ and proper maps $W_{abj}\to U_{abj}$. For each fixed $(a,b)$ the $W_{abj}$ cover $T\times_{S_1}S_a$ by the relative open-cover clause of the cited statement. The generic field $k(T)/K$ is finite separable. Crucially this node applies to arbitrary integral qcqs schemes, unlike the finite-type-over-$\mathbf Z$ statement of lem-trf-riemann-zariski-finite-refinement.

source.place: Theorem 3.5.5, Steps 1 and 5, using Propositions 3.2.1,3.2.6 and Corollary 3.2.7, printed pp. 15–17,22,24.

proof.text: Pull each $Y_{abj}$ back to $W_{abj}$, obtaining a finite map $Q_{abj}\to H_{abj}:=Z_{ab}\times_{S_a}W_{abj}$; finiteness survives by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange]. The $H_{abj}$ are quasi-compact opens covering $Z_T:=Z\times_{S_1}T$: for any point of $Z_T$, first choose its chart $Z_{ab}$ and then a $W_{abj}$ containing its base point. Flatness and finite presentation of $Q_{abj}\to W_{abj}$ survive by [lem-pc-relatively-flat-module-pullback] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](3), and reduced geometric fibres by [lem-trf-geometric-reduced-fibre-locus-base-change]. Viewed over $T$, each $Q_{abj}$ is flat because $W_{abj}\subseteq T$ has the same local rings, and locally of finite presentation because affine charts in $W_{abj}$ are affine charts in $T$. It is qcqs by the cited permanence lemma (2), and its map to the qcqs $T$ is therefore finitely presented by (1). Fibres outside $W_{abj}$ are empty, hence reduced. Each map agrees with $H_{abj}$ on the generic fibre.

source.place: Theorem 3.5.5, Step 5, base change of local constructions before gluing, printed p. 24.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-finite-eta-modification-gluing] to the flat finitely presented family $Z_T\to T$ and its finite quasi-compact open covering by the $H_{abj}$, with the maps $Q_{abj}\to H_{abj}$. It gives an integral finite proper surjective birational modification $S'\to T$ after which the local finite maps have unique overlap identifications satisfying the cocycle condition. They glue to a finite map $Y'\to Z\times_{S_1}S'$ that is a generic isomorphism; $Y'\to S'$ is flat and finitely presented with reduced geometric fibres. There is no application of eta-normality to $T$ or $S'$. The additional finite base modification, supplied by the gluing lemma, replaces the unjustified immediate uniqueness claim of the returned step 5.

source.place: Corollary 3.5.4 and Theorem 3.5.5, Steps 1 and 5, printed pp. 21–22,24.

proof.text: Set $r$ to be the composite $S'\to T\to S_1\to S$. Properness follows from [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]; surjectivity is preserved by composition, and the three maps are surjective (the model $T\to S_1$ is proper dominant, so its image is closed and contains the generic point). Since the first and third maps have trivial generic field extension, $r_\eta=\operatorname{Spec}k(T)$ with $k(T)/K$ finite separable. The base change of $a$ is finite by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange], so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] makes the composite $q:Y'\to Z\times_{S_1}S'\to X\times_SS'$ finite. Both arrows induce the specified generic isomorphisms, hence so does $q$. All flatness, finite-presentation and reduced-geometric-fibre conclusions are those of step 7.

source.place: Theorem 3.5.5, assembly of Steps 0–5, printed pp. 21–24.

proof.text: Finally the generic fibre is schematically dense in $Y'$. Over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S'$ with $R$ a domain, apply [lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free] to any open of its inverse image with the invertible module $\mathcal O$. If a section restricts to zero on the generic fibre, then on each affine chart some nonzero $s\in R$ annihilates it (generic restriction is localization at $R\setminus\{0\}$). The cited injectivity forces the section to vanish. Covering the open by these charts proves the assertion. This argument concerns the flat source $Y'$ and requires no normality of the altered base.

source.place: Elementary generic-density verification after Theorem 3.5.5, using flatness over an integral base.

statement_change.what: The dense-isomorphism-open clause is false for a dominant nonflat input. Take S=Spec k[t] and X=S disjoint union Spec k at t=0. The generic fibre is Spec k(t), reduced geometrically. After any proper surjective alteration of the integral base the vertical component remains nonempty. A schematically dense target open must meet it; an isomorphism over that open forces a nonempty open of the flat source to be killed by the nonzero base element t, impossible over an integral base. Temkin §3.5 expressly uses a proper generic-fibre isomorphism for nonflat inputs. Remove just the unsupported dense-open clause, and the proof passages asserting it.

Properness follows from [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]; surjectivity is preserved by composition, and the three maps are surjective (the model $T\to S_1$ is proper dominant, so its image is closed and contains the generic point). Since the first and third maps have trivial generic field extension, $r_\eta=\operatorname{Spec}k(T)$ with $k(T)/K$ finite separable. The base change of $a$ is finite by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange], so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] makes the composite $q:Y'\to Z\times_{S_1}S'\to X\times_SS'$ finite. The dense isomorphism open from Step 7 pulls back along the finite eta-modification $a$ and is combined with the dense open from Step 1; their intersection is schematically dense on both sides, and $q$ is an isomorphism there. Both arrows induce the specified generic isomorphisms, hence so does $q$. All flatness, finite-presentation and reduced-geometric-fibre conclusions are those of step 7.

old_proof.text: Finally the generic fibre is schematically dense in $Y'$. Over an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S'$ with $R$ a domain, apply [lem-sc-flat-invertible-sections-torsion-free] to any open of its inverse image with the invertible module $\mathcal O$. If a section restricts to zero on the generic fibre, then on each affine chart some nonzero $s\in R$ annihilates it (generic restriction is localization at $R\setminus\{0\}$). The cited injectivity forces the section to vanish. Covering the open by these charts proves the assertion. This argument concerns the flat source $Y'$ and requires no normality of the altered base.
